text:
Maya: Quick sync — planning to flip feature flag `burst_queueing` to enable queueing fallback on prod next Tue 09:00 PT. Need sign-off on scope, canary audience, and rollback guardrails.

Maya: Proposed rollout: canary -> 5% internal traffic for 30m, promote to 20% for 30m, then full. Scope: only model_family=redwood-v1; exclude enterprise customers. Guardrails to watch: p99 token latency < 1200ms, request error rate < 0.5%, queue depth < 200, no increase in eviction rate.

Maya: Steps (quick):
```bash
# set canary audience
redwoodctl flags set burst_queueing=true --env=prod --audience=canary-5pct
# promote
redwoodctl flags promote burst_queueing --to 20pct
# full
redwoodctl flags promote burst_queueing --to 100pct
```

Liam: Quick Q — can we scope the canary by model config (redwood-v1) and also pin quantization profile to fp16 for canary nodes? want to avoid perf noise from mixed q configs. Who's primary oncall for 09:00-10:00 PT?

Selena: I can take primary. +1 on limiting to redwood-v1. Also strongly suggest excluding any enterprise tenants (billing/customer-id tag) so we don't risk SLA customers. Recommend a fallback route to small-models if queueing depth spikes.

Tom: Ops note: set autoscaler max_concurrency guardrail to 100 for canary nodes. Add an automated rollback trigger: if queue depth > 150 for 10m OR p50 latency > 2x baseline for 5m -> rollback to previous flag state. I'll leave a short runbook snippet below.

Tom: Runbook snippet:
```
If metrics breach during rollout:
  - run: redwoodctl flags set burst_queueing=false --env=prod --audience=all
  - notify: #incidents + oncall (pager)
  - validate: ensure queue_depth < 50 and p99 latency returns to baseline
  - postmortem: capture traces for top 10 hosts by queue depth
```

deploy-bot: Canary dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/abc123/canary-burst-queueing?orgId=1 (watch: p99_token_latency, queue_depth, error_rate, eviction_rate)

Maya: Thanks — Liam, can you prepare the LD/flag targeting PR and include the exclusion for enterprise customers? Selena/Tom please be on standby Tue 09:00 PT for the first promotion. If no objections by EOD Fri I'll schedule the toggle. :thumbsup:

Liam: Will do. I'll open PR and add the quantization pin. ETA EOD Thu.

Selena: LGTM, I'll block time on my calendar.

Tom: I'll monitor autoscaler and leave 30m of extra capacity in the pool for the canary window.

Maya: Great — marking as planned unless someone raises a blocker. If anything changes I'll update here.

Liam: one more question — should we run a quick smoke that injects synthetic traffic to the canary audience before promoting to 20%?

Selena: yes please. run synthetic for 10m at expected 5% throughput and validate no backlog growth.

Tom: I'll script the synthetic load and post the command tomorrow.

Maya: Awesome. Thanks all.
